fatal_errors: The reported 13.5% terminal strain is treated as the baseline tensile uniform elongation, although it was reported with compressive properties and does not establish a tensile uniform-elongation baseline.
The requested matched compression, tension, and impact test program is incomplete because no matched compression test is included.
Hot-rolling reduction, annealing temperature and duration, tensile strain rate, and impact strain-rate limits are not specified, making the intervention insufficiently reproducible.
Preservation of energetic performance is asserted without a material-specific mechanism connecting grain refinement or a bimodal microstructure to fragmentation and oxidation in HfZrTiTa0.53.
explanation: The proposal addresses the strength–ductility objective and offers a testable thermomechanical-processing alternative, but it does not reconstruct the target Ta-Nb-V alloying strategy or its HCP-to-BCC/omega-phase mechanism. Its cited evidence shows that rolling and heat treatment can improve strength–ductility balance in other multicomponent alloys, but neither study validates a bimodal microstructure, greater than 20% elongation, or retained impact energy release in HfZrTiTa0.53. The baseline conflates terminal compressive strain with tensile uniform elongation, so the quantitative improvement and falsification threshold are not validly anchored. Room-temperature tension and impact controls are proposed, but loading rates and processing parameters are vague, compression is omitted, and thin-target penetration is not matched to the approximately 4000 s^-1 SHPB-in-air energy-release condition of the target study.
